partner_result.application: Used directly to convert the preserved three-bank core M+tau alpha alpha^T into the density bound 296/s_min, with arbitrary outside quadratic completion and no independence assumption.

new_results.statement: For an exact partner-type three-bank core M, a rank-one addition tau(v^T X)^2 whose restriction to each bank is alpha_j u_j preserves the exact representation with core M+tau alpha alpha^T. The partner theorem gives density <296/s_min(M+tau alpha alpha^T). Weyl gives <296/(eta s0) if |tau| ||alpha||^2 <=(1-eta)s0; for M>=s0 I and tau>=0 there is no loss at any magnitude; for tau=-beta and beta alpha^T M^{-1}alpha<=1-eta, the same eta-loss bound holds.

For every real tau and epsilon>0 there are arbitrarily large n and A with spectrum {1,1,1,tau,0,...} for which every exact three-disjoint-one-scalar-bank representation has s_min(M)<epsilon. Fourier modes 0,1 form the rank-three projector and an orthogonal mode-2 vector carries eigenvalue tau. Generic phase for tau<0 makes every physical 2x2 principal block nonsingular, forcing singleton banks; then s_min(M)<=3(3+2|tau|)/n. Taking tau_n=+/-sqrt(n) keeps the exact-bank scale tending to zero despite an unbounded fourth eigenvalue of either sign.

unresolved_implication: The spectral hypothesis alone does not force a uniformly conditioned exact one-scalar-per-bank core. The next bridge must use approximate or overlapping bank aggregation, multiple statistics per bank, or a joint error payment before reciprocal conditioning.
next_step: Quantify an approximate multi-statistic bank version of the partner theorem on diffuse Parseval/Fourier frames, retaining original-coordinate product provenance and charging factorization error in mixed norm rather than by worst local s_min.
